items.problem: `copy_text` of an empty string in a headless run of `QACore` (or on a platform without a clipboard) matches two rows of `## error` (lines 117 and 118) with different log levels (error and warn), and `## behavior` lists the three conditions without an order, so the log level of that call differs per implementation

The condition under which `request_review` of the adapter reports a failure is set only for `android` (line 62). For `ios` and `macos` (`SKStoreReviewController`, line 52-53), whether the adapter reports a failure (e.g. no foreground window scene for the scene-taking request call) or always reports success is not set, so the `Failed` row of `## error` (line 111) can differ per implementation on those platforms

`Throttled` is set by "its difference from the current device time is less than `NativeUiCore.reviewMinIntervalMs`", but the sign of the difference is not set. Device time can be changed by the user (time-core.md:58). When the device clock is set back so that `last_review_at` is later than the current device time by more than `reviewMinIntervalMs`, a signed difference (now − `last_review_at`, negative) gives `Throttled`, while an absolute difference gives `Requested`; with `last_review_at` − now (the literal reading of "its difference from") every call would be `Throttled`. Existed before this change; the spec changes diff is empty

The browser runtime `share` calls `navigator.share` through `JavaScriptBridge`, but which promise rejections become `Closed` and which become `Failed` (`AbortError` when the user dismisses the sheet, `NotAllowedError` without transient user activation, `DataError`) is not set, and neither is whether `supports_share(true)` (image) on `web` depends on `navigator.canShare({files})`. native-ui-core.md:54 says only that share is none when the browser does not provide the API, so `ShareResult` for the same browser action differs per implementation. Existed before this change; the spec changes diff is empty
